name: Clinical Psychologist
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: The regulated clinical psychology route: psychology degree, master’s, RCI-recognised M.Phil and licence to practise.

phases.title: Class 11–12: lay the foundation
phases.summary: Any stream works; Psychology, Biology and English help.
points: Choose Psychology if your school offers it; Biology and Statistics also help.
Read about mental health, behaviour and development from reliable sources.
Volunteer or observe in school counselling or helpline settings where possible.
Be prepared for a long, structured training path.

phases.title: Bachelor’s degree in Psychology
phases.summary: BA or BSc Psychology builds the foundation.
points: Take admission through CUET-UG or merit at a recognised university.
Study developmental, social, cognitive, abnormal and counselling psychology, plus research methods and statistics.
Do internships in clinics, schools or NGOs.
Aim for strong marks, since the next stage is competitive.

phases.title: Master’s in Psychology
points: Apply through CUET-PG or university tests.
Choose a university with good clinical exposure and supervision.
Complete practicals, case studies and a dissertation.
Some universities offer MA/MSc Clinical Psychology, which is the best preparation.

phases.title: M.Phil in Clinical Psychology (RCI-recognised)
phases.summary: A two-year supervised clinical programme, the professional qualification.
points: Apply to RCI-recognised institutions such as NIMHANS, CIP Ranchi, AIIMS, IHBAS and others through their own entrance tests.
Training combines coursework, supervised assessments, therapy and a dissertation.
Clinical rotations include adult, child and neuropsychology placements.
This M.Phil is required to be recognised as a clinical psychologist under RCI rules.

phases.title: RCI registration and practice
phases.summary: Register with the Rehabilitation Council of India and begin practice.
points: Apply to RCI for a Registration (CRR) number as a clinical psychologist.
Work in hospitals, mental health institutes, private clinics, schools or NGOs.
Follow ethical and legal standards under the Mental Healthcare Act.
Further study: PhD, specialised training in therapy or neuropsychology.
